newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-IRVINE IN CHARGE AS FERRARI HEAD PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-IRVINE IN CHARGE AS FERRARI HEAD PRACTICE.

text.p: Eddie Irvine sent Ferrari's army of followers into raptures on Friday when he produced the fastest lap ever recorded at Imola during practice for Sunday's San Marino Grand Prix.

The British driver, a strong second behind Jacques Villeneuve in Argentina two weeks ago and troubled by subsequent threats against his family in Northern Ireland, relegated illustrious team mate Michael Schumacher to second place.
Irvine was ahead of Germany's double world champion as he clocked a best lap of one minute 25.981 seconds.
Their joint performance on Ferrari's home circuit, the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari, boosted the spirits of their fans and raised hopes that the team can now claim a first win of the year.

Irvine, whose family received threatening phones calls because of the Irish flag which was raised in his honour in Buenos Aires, put the worry behind him with a performance that proved he is recovering well from a shaky start to the year.
After failing to score a point in Australia or Brazil, Irvine cut nearly a second off the existing track best of 1:26.890 set by Schumacher last year.
Gerhard Berger, who on Sunday will contest his 200th grand prix, and his Benetton team mate Jean Alesi were third and fourth fastest respectively.
World championship leader Villeneuve was fifth in his Williams and David Coulthard in a McLaren sixth.

Irvine admitted that his time was not hugely significant and said: "I struggled a bit this morning. The tyres have so much grip that sometimes I would go very deep into the chicanes before scrubbing off speed.
"Between the two sessions, I thought about how to improve the car and halfway through the afternoon we made a big step forward.
"But this track is much harder on brakes than Melbourne and that has caused me a few problems. But it will not be a problem in the race."

Schumacher was more optimistic for Ferrari. He said: "We are in better shape here than we were in the last race in Argentina, but we don't know if our main rivals fitted new tyres today. And they may have had more fuel. But we did a good job and now we need to find an even better set-up for qualifying tomorrow."

Villeneuve admitted he was disappointed and said he felt he could go much quicker. "We had an engine problem this morning which cost us some time and we spent a lot of time on the brakes. It is a tough track for brakes."
